newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON FORCES CRITICS TO EAT THEIR WORDS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON FORCES CRITICS TO EAT THEIR WORDS.

text.p: Michael Johnson brought back golden memories of Gothenburg and Atlanta when he powrered to a truly memorable victory in the world 400 metres final on Tuesday.
For once, his success, achieved in 44.12 seconds of controlled clinical superiority, was not just awesome for the way he performed on the track.

It was a victory forged as much in his heart and mind, ending weeks of speculation that he was no longer the invincible force who won 200 and 400 metres doubles at the world championships in Gothenburg in 1995 and the Olympics a year ago. It was also his third successive world championship 400 title.
Troubled since June 1 by an injury sustained in his ill- fated 150 metres head-to-head with Donovan Bailey in Toronto, Johnson has had to endure a disrupted period of preparation for Athens.

Cynics were convinced there were chinks in his armour after he misjudged the finish of his second round qualifier and only reached the semifinal as one of the fastest losers. They could not have been more wrong.

Johnson eased his way through the opening 200, run through a cramp attack which lasted for a few seconds around the final bend and then blitzed past the field to win in 44.12 seconds, a time none of the other finalists have ever achieved.

Ugandan Davis Kamoga, who won the bronze at Atlanta, took the silver in 44.37 seconds, while American Tyree Washington, who openly questioned Johnson's heart for the battle on Monday, finished third in 44.39. "He has heart now alright," admitted
Washington, "He wanted to prove something tonight and he did."
Johnson, allowed to take part here as a defending champion despite missing the U.S. trials, celebrated his victory by holding a Superman T-shirt on an uncharacteristically joyous victory lap.
"A fan gave it to me," he laughed afterwards, fully realising the symbolism of the act.
"It's been a tough season though, and I am really pleased to be back and healthy again. I thought that perhaps I could have gone a little faster, but a win is a win.
"I would not have come if I didn't think I could have won it and today I always knew I was going to do just that."

The race was oozing with quality and ended with seven of the eight finalists running under 44.60 seconds. Kamoga set a national record and Washington, Mark Richardson of Britain and Antonio Pettigrew of the United States, the 1991 world chanmpion, ran the fastest times of their lives.
Johnson, as a result of his wild card status, was one of four Americans in the field which also comprised three Britons and the Ugandan.

Britain's Iwan Thomas and Kamoga made all the early runnig before Johnson took control of the race 100 metres from home, powering away as unstoppable as ever down the home straight, accelerating clear of the field to win with ease.
